name: Pure lands and buddha-fields

definitions.definition: Sukhāvatī lies west beyond ten trillion lands; it surpasses the three realms and is not included in them; it is the reward of Dharmākara's vows; Amitābha became buddha there ten kalpas ago; its 29 adornments are the object of contemplation.

relations.note: the Western land with direction and form vs the land that is pure where the mind is pure; later Chinese masters hold both

name: Dharmākara's forty-eight vows

definitions.definition: Tanluan singles out three vows as proof of other-power — the 18th (birth by ten recitations), 11th (rightly established group), 22nd (surpassing the stages; returning to save beings); the Sanskrit recension has 47 vows.
Shinran reads five 'true' vows (11th, 12th, 13th, 17th, 18th) and the provisional 19th and 20th, and the 22nd for the returning aspect.

name: The eighteenth (primal) vow

names.name: the vow of sincere mind and entrusting

definitions.definition: Read by Shandao as 'beings who call my name even ten times'; the exclusion of grave offenders is a gate of restraint.
The vow that selected the nenbutsu alone as the practice for birth.
The vow of sincere mind and entrusting (shinjin), whose three minds are one mind given by Amida; the cause of birth in the true land.

name: The nine grades of birth in Sukhāvatī

definitions.definition: For Shandao all nine grades are ordinary beings differing by good or evil conditions met, not sages of the stages; the three minds are required of all.
The nine grades belong to the 'essential gate' of self-power good leading to the transformed land.

name: Rejoicing in and dedicating merit

definitions.definition: The fifth gate: never abandoning suffering beings, making transfer foremost; of two aspects, going and returning.
The transfer is Amida's, not the practitioner's: the nenbutsu is 'non-transferring' practice.

name: Other-power (tali / tariki)

definitions.definition: The power of Amitābha's original vow as the dominant condition of birth and of all that follows; the easy path rides on it (Tanluan).
Birth through the nenbutsu that accords with the Buddha's vow; the practitioner keeps calling.
Wholly Amida's working: shinjin and the nenbutsu are given; the practitioner's 'no working is true working'.

relations.note: analogous only: in both, liberation is effected by another's power; Pure Land posits no creator Lord and Shinshū denies that Amida is a god among gods
analogous: total reliance on the saviour's vow / surrender to the Lord as the means; the Shinshū 'no calculation' resembles the Tenkalai 'cat' view

name: Self-power (zili / jiriki)

definitions.definition: Reliance on one's own practice for non-retrogression — the difficult path, hard in an age without a buddha.
Reliance on one's own good and calculation, including self-power nenbutsu; leads to the transformed land.

name: The easy path and the difficult path

definitions.definition: The bodhisattva path has a difficult way of strenuous effort (like walking overland) and an easy way of faith and calling buddhas' names (like sailing); Tanluan identifies the easy way with birth by the Buddha's vow.
Shinran's first master Nāgārjuna 'taught the easy practice'.

name: The two gates: the holy path and the Pure Land

definitions.definition: Of two excellent dharmas, the holy path (awakening in this world by one's own practice) is hard to realise in the last age; only the Pure Land gate is passable (Daochuo).
Set aside the holy path and enter the Pure Land gate (Senchakushū 1, 16).
Compassion of the path of sages is limited; that of the Pure Land path is thoroughgoing (Tannishō 4); the 'two pairs and four levels' refine the division.

relations.note: Daochuo's two gates restate Nāgārjuna's two paths in terms of the age

name: The three ages of the Dharma (true, semblance, final)

definitions.definition: After the Buddha's passing the Dharma declines through periods (the Candragarbha's five five-hundred-year periods; true, semblance and final ages); teaching must fit the time; in the last age calling the name is the main practice.
The true and semblance ages are over; in the last age there are only nominal monks; the Larger Sūtra alone remains after the scriptures perish.
Following Daochuo, the holy path does not suit the last age; the nenbutsu alone remains after the scriptures perish (Senchakushū 1, 6).

members: extinction of the Dharma (fametsu), after which the Larger Sūtra remains a hundred years

relations.note: partial: Indian accounts of the Dharma's decline (Sarvāstivāda) vs the East Asian three-age scheme; the counting differs

name: Teaching fitted to time and capacity

definitions.definition: A teaching that fits the time and the capacity of beings is easy to practise and awaken by; one that does not is like drilling wet wood for fire (Daochuo).

name: Birth in the Pure Land (wangsheng / ōjō) as the condition for awakening

definitions.definition: At death the practitioner is born by transformation in a lotus in Sukhāvatī, where he is non-retrogressive, sees the Buddha, hears the Dharma and completes the path — then returns to save beings.
Birth at death through the nenbutsu, with the Buddha's welcome; awakening is attained there.
Birth in the true land is at once the attainment of great nirvāṇa; it is settled in this life at the moment of shinjin.

name: The birth of non-birth

names.name: wusheng zhi sheng 無生之生

definitions.definition: Birth in the Pure Land arises from the pure vow and is not the deluded birth of the three existences; dharma-nature is unborn and 'birth' is said from the side of those born; the wise seek birth ardently while knowing birth has no own-being (Tanluan, Daochuo, Jingtu shiyi lun, Chuandeng).

relations.note: reconciled by the tradition itself through the two truths: birth conventionally, non-arising ultimately

name: The Pure Land as mind only (weixin jingtu)

definitions.definition: Mind, Buddha and beings are one; the Western land is born within one's own mind (Zunshi); every land is the Bliss of mind-only and every buddha the Amitābha of one's nature (Tianru); yet one must be born in a buddha-land because one's power is insufficient (Yanshou), and to deny the Western land while unable to live in a latrine without disgust is self-deception (Zhuhong).
Not accepted: the Pure Land is pointed to in a direction and given form for ordinary beings.

relations.note: the Pure Land application of 'this mind makes the Buddha'
held together with, not instead of, the Western land by Yanshou and Zhuhong

name: Dual cultivation of Chan and Pure Land (chanjing shuangxiu)

definitions.definition: Chan and Pure Land reach the same end by different roads; 'Chan is the Chan of Pure Land, Pure Land the Pure Land of Chan'; practise one gate deeply; Yanshou's myriad good practices include recitation. The 'four alternatives' ascribed to Yanshou (with Chan and Pure Land like a tiger with horns) are a later formulation.
In Chan contexts recitation is used as a huatou ('who is reciting the Buddha's name?') or as a practice for those of lesser capacity (as reported in the Pure Land sources).

notes: The Chan side is contributed only as reported in Pure Land texts; U42 owns the Chan definitions.

name: The five gates of mindfulness (wu nianmen)

definitions.definition: Worship (body), praise and calling the name (speech), aspiration = śamatha, contemplation = vipaśyanā of the 29 adornments, and transfer of merit; they bring the five gates of merit (approach, great assembly, dwelling, chamber, garden of play), the last being the return to teach.
Read by Shinran as Amida's practice transferred to beings, not the practitioner's.

name: The twenty-nine adornments of Sukhāvatī

definitions.definition: Seventeen adornments of the land, eight of the Buddha, four of the bodhisattvas; together they enter the one dharma-phrase.

members: 17 of the land (purity, measure, nature, form, manifold things, colour, touch, water/ground/space, rain, light, sound, lord, retinue, enjoyment, no difficulties, gate of the great meaning, fulfilment of wishes)
8 of the Buddha (seat, body, speech, mind, assembly, leader, lord, unfailing sustaining power)

name: The two dharma-bodies (of dharma-nature and of expedient means)

definitions.definition: From the dharma-body of dharma-nature arises the dharma-body of expedient means, which manifests the former; different but inseparable (Tanluan); the adornments enter the one phrase, the uncreated dharma-body of true wisdom (Vasubandhu).
From the formless dharma-body as suchness appeared Dharmākara, who became Amida; Amida is the means to know jinen.

relations.note: a two-body analysis of the buddha as reality and as saving form, beside the three-body scheme

name: Sukhāvatī as a reward land into which ordinary beings are born

definitions.definition: Amitābha is a reward-body buddha and Sukhāvatī a reward land, not a transformation land (Daochuo); though lofty, ordinary beings enter it by the power of the vow (Shandao).

name: True and transformed lands; womb-birth and the borderland

definitions.definition: Those who aspire with doubt of the Buddha's wisdom are born in palaces or closed lotuses where for five hundred years they do not see the Buddha — womb-birth or the borderland; those of mixed practice stop in the land of sloth and pride.

The true land (of immeasurable light) is reached by other-power shinjin; self-power practitioners of the 19th and 20th vows are born in the transformed land (womb-palace, borderland, realm of indolence, castle of doubt).

name: Non-retrogression of those born in Sukhāvatī

definitions.definition: Those born cannot fall back, for five reasons: the vow's power, the Buddha's light, the teaching of the birds and trees, the company of bodhisattvas only, and a life as long as the buddhas' (Jingtu shiyi lun); unlike Tuṣita.

name: The rightly established state (zhengding ju / shōjōju)

definitions.definition: Those born in the Pure Land dwell in the rightly established group and necessarily reach nirvāṇa (11th vow); recollecting Amitābha one enters the stage of certainty (Nāgārjuna).
Entered in this life, at the one thought-moment of shinjin; the person is 'equal to the Tathāgatas', 'the same as Maitreya'.

relations.note: in China placed after birth, in Shinran before death

name: The ten recitations (shinian / jūnen)

definitions.definition: Ten continuous thoughts or voicings of Amitābha at death suffice even for evil-doers because their weight lies in mind, object and decisiveness; they need not be counted (Tanluan, Daochuo); read as ten voicings (Shandao); as ten breaths each morning (Zunshi).

name: The three minds of the Contemplation Sūtra

definitions.definition: Sincere mind, deep mind (true entrusting of two kinds) and the mind of dedicating merit and aspiring; with these one is surely born, lacking one, not (Shandao).
The settled mind (anjin) of the nenbutsu practitioner, contained in the conviction of birth.

members: mind of dedicating merit and aspiring (huixiang fayuan xin)

name: The three minds of the eighteenth vow (sincere mind, entrusting, aspiration)

definitions.definition: Shishin (sincere mind), shingyō (entrusting with joy) and yokushō (aspiration for birth) are Amida's true mind given to beings and are one mind, shinjin.

relations.note: Shinran distinguishes the self-power three minds of the Contemplation Sūtra from those of the vow

name: The two kinds of deep entrusting (nishu jinshin)

definitions.definition: Deep entrusting that one is an ordinary being without escape, and that Amitābha's vow surely saves.
The structure of shinjin: entrusting concerning the person (ki) and concerning the Dharma (hō).

members: entrusting concerning the person (ki no jinshin)
entrusting concerning the Dharma (hō no jinshin)

name: The five right practices and the rightly determined act

definitions.definition: Reading the Pure Land sūtras, contemplating, worshipping, calling the name, praising and offering — all directed to Amitābha; calling the name is the rightly determined act, the others auxiliary.
Set aside the auxiliary and choose the rightly determined act.

members: calling the name (chengming) — the rightly determined act

name: Exclusive and miscellaneous practice

definitions.definition: Exclusive practice: ten of ten are born; mixed practice: one or two in a hundred, for thirteen reasons of lost right mindfulness and non-accord with the vow (Shandao); the mixed stop in the land of sloth (Huaigan).
Right and miscellaneous differ in five pairs; cast aside the miscellaneous.

name: The four modes of practice (sixiu)

definitions.definition: Reverent, exclusive, uninterrupted and long-lasting practice, to be kept until the end of life (Shandao).
The 'manner of practice' (sagyō), contained in the conviction of birth.

name: Meditative and non-meditative good

definitions.definition: The Contemplation Sūtra's first thirteen contemplations are meditative good, the three meritorious acts and nine grades non-meditative good — Śākyamuni's 'essential gate'; the Buddha's intent, however, is the calling of the name ('universal vow').

name: The parable of the two rivers and the white path

definitions.definition: A traveller between a river of fire (anger) and of water (greed) crosses a narrow white path (the aspiration for birth) urged by Śākyamuni from the east and called by Amitābha from the west (Shandao).
Shinran reads the white path as other-power shinjin and the voices as the two Honoured Ones' command and call.

name: The selected primal vow (senchaku hongan)

definitions.definition: Dharmākara selected the nenbutsu alone as the practice of the primal vow, because the name contains all virtues and is easy for all; Śākyamuni and all buddhas likewise selected it.
Shandao: looking to the Buddha's primal vow, its intent is that beings exclusively call Amitābha's name.

name: The name contains all virtues

definitions.definition: The name of the Tathāgata of Unhindered Light breaks all ignorance and fulfils all aspirations when called in accord with reality (Tanluan); hearing the name with joy even for one thought gains unsurpassed merit.
The name gathers all the virtues of the Buddha's inner realization and outer activity, as 'house' contains all its timbers (Senchakushū 3).
The auspicious name embodying all virtues is the great practice.

relations.note: analogous doctrines of the saving power of a divine / buddha name; the Pure Land grounds it in a buddha's vow, the Hindu traditions in the identity of name and named

name: The name as itself birth (Ippen)

definitions.definition: Birth for all was settled as Namu Amida Butsu at Amida's awakening; the name itself is birth; the practitioner casts off even faith and simply says it.

name: Interfusion of one and all in the nenbutsu (yūzū)

definitions.definition: One person is all people and all people one; one practice all practices; the nenbutsu of each interfuses with all — birth by other-power.

name: Shinjin — true entrusting

definitions.definition: The mind of entrusting to the primal vow, free of doubt, given by Amida; the true cause of birth; buddha-nature; arising in one thought-moment, it brings the benefit of being embraced and the rightly established state; it is hard to attain not because the practice is hard but because shinjin is hard.

relations.note: Shinran identifies great shinjin with buddha-nature (quoting the Nirvāṇa Sūtra)

name: The evil person as the true object of the vow (akunin shōki)

definitions.definition: The vow was made for beings full of passions who cannot free themselves; those who rely on their own good are not its object until they turn; hence 'even the good person attains birth, how much more the evil person'. This is not licence: poison is not to be taken because there is an antidote.
Even the evil-doer of the lowest grade is born by ten recitations at death (Contemplation Sūtra, Daochuo).

name: Jinen hōni (naturalness by the working of the vow)

definitions.definition: Being made so of itself by the vow, without calculation; the formless supreme Buddha is jinen; Amida is the means to know it; 'no working is true working'.

name: Neither monk nor layman (hisō hizoku) and the married clergy

definitions.definition: After laicisation Shinran called himself neither monk nor layman; Shinshū clergy marry; in the last age only nominal monks remain and are still to be honoured; one does not worship other deities for worldly benefit.
Hōnen: live in whatever way lets you best say the nenbutsu — as a hijiri or married.

name: Precepts and the nenbutsu

definitions.definition: Chinese Pure Land joins recitation with precepts and good conduct: the three meritorious acts; Mao Ziyuan's five precepts confirmed by five recitations; Yinguang's 'fulfil your duties, avoid evil'.

Precepts are not the condition of birth (they are not the selected practice), yet disciples must not claim the nenbutsu has no precepts or encourages evil (Seven-Article Pledge); Jōdo-shū transmits the bodhisattva precepts.
No precepts in the last age; licensed evil is nevertheless rejected.

name: The nenbutsu as gratitude (hōon)

definitions.definition: Once shinjin is settled, the nenbutsu is said in gratitude for Amida's benevolence, not as a cause of birth.

name: Oneness of person and Dharma (kihō ittai)

definitions.definition: In Namu Amida Butsu the person who entrusts and the Dharma that saves are one; the Buddha's attainment and beings' birth were accomplished together (Anjin ketsujōshō; Rennyo).
Associated with the Seizan milieu of the Anjin ketsujōshō (attribution uncertain).

name: The one great matter of the afterlife (goshō no ichidaiji)

definitions.definition: Life is fleeting — rosy cheeks in the morning, white ashes in the evening; take to heart the matter of the life to come and rely on Amida.

name: The law of the land and the Buddha's Dharma (ōbō / buppō)

definitions.definition: Keep the law of the land as fundamental and humanity and justice first, while keeping shinjin within; do not disparage other buddhas and kami (Rennyo).

name: The ordinary foolish being (fanfu / bonbu)

definitions.definition: The Contemplation Sūtra was taught for ordinary beings of feeble mind like Vaidehī; all nine grades are ordinary beings; one must deeply know oneself as an ordinary being without escape.
The foolish being full of blind passions to the end, without a single true mind; the very object of the vow.
Hōnen, finding himself unable to keep precepts, meditation or wisdom, took the path for ignorant ordinary people and taught the learned to behave like those who know not a letter.

name: The samādhi of recollecting the Buddha

definitions.definition: The king of samādhis, in which the Buddha and his assembly are seen clearly before one's eyes; reached through contemplation or through continuous (and loud) recitation; a seven-day hall practice.

name: Seeing the Buddha (jianfo) in samādhi, dream or at death

definitions.definition: The Buddha is seen by the three powers of his vow, the samādhi and one's merit; Huiyuan saw him three times and at death; visions seen should not be told lightly — good ones are known to oneself, bad ones repented (Shandao).
Shinshū does not seek visions: though passions blind us and we cannot see him, the Buddha's compassion always illumines us.

name: Auspicious signs of birth at death

definitions.definition: The biographies of those born record light, fragrance, heavenly music, purple clouds, visions of the Buddha and foreknowledge of the time of death; Zunshi's vow asks to know the time, be free of pain and die as if in samādhi.
Not relied on: the person of shinjin is settled regardless of the manner of death (letter 1).

name: The five augmenting conditions of reciting (Shandao)

definitions.definition: Extinction of sins, protection and long life, seeing the Buddha, being embraced, and the testimony of birth.

name: The benefits in the present life (genze riyaku / genshō jūyaku)

definitions.definition: Ten benefits of the person of shinjin, from protection by unseen beings to entry into the rightly established state; the hymns on benefits in this life.
Shandao's augmenting conditions include long life and protection in this life.

name: Embraced, never to be abandoned (shequ bu she)

definitions.definition: Each ray of Amitāyus's light shines through the ten directions and embraces the beings who recollect him.
At the moment the thought of saying the nenbutsu arises in entrusting, one shares in being embraced.

name: The difficulty of faith in the easy practice

definitions.definition: The arrogant and lazy can hardly believe this teaching; to hear and entrust is the hardest of hard things.
The practice is easy but shinjin hard; 'easy to go, yet no one goes'.

name: Turning through the three vows (sangan tennyū)

definitions.definition: From the 19th vow (various goods, welcome at death) through the 20th (self-power nenbutsu) to the 18th (other-power shinjin).

name: Two pairs and four levels (nisō shijū)

definitions.definition: Vertical transcending, vertical going out, crosswise going out, crosswise transcending; the primal vow is crosswise transcendence.

name: The two aspects of merit transfer: going and returning

definitions.definition: Going: dedicating merit to be born together with all beings; returning: coming back from the Pure Land to teach (Tanluan; Vasubandhu's fifth gate; 22nd vow).
Both are Amida's transfer to beings.

name: The aspiration for awakening in Pure Land teaching

definitions.definition: The aspiration to become a buddha is the aspiration to save beings; one who seeks birth only for pleasure is not born (Tanluan); beginners seek birth first because they cannot yet save beings in the evil world.
Not a separate requirement of birth in Hōnen's reading (disputed by Myōe).
Other-power bodhicitta is shinjin.

name: Loathing this defiled world, joyfully seeking the Pure Land

names.name: enri edo, gongu jōdo 厭離穢土・欣求浄土

definitions.definition: Vaidehī's turning from this evil world; the three realms as a dark house to be loathed; two practices of loathing (impurity contemplation) and joyful aspiration; Genshin's first two chapters.

name: Deathbed practice and right mindfulness at death

definitions.definition: The dying person faces west, fixes mind and voice on Amitābha; companions recite with him, record and repent visions; those who have taken wine or meat keep away; friends pledge in advance to help one another complete the ten recitations; do not move or weep over the dying.
The person of shinjin does not depend on the manner of death or deathbed rites.

relations.note: analogous emphasis on the state of mind at death (BhG 8.5-6 and the Purāṇas / the ten recitations); the Pure Land relies on the Buddha's welcome, not on the thought alone

name: The Buddha's welcome at death (raigō)

definitions.definition: Amitābha and the holy assembly appear before the dying practitioner (19th vow; Smaller Sūtra); Huiyuan's vision before death.
The nenbutsu practitioner is welcomed at death (Senchakushū; the raigō paintings).
Belongs to those of various practices; not awaited by the person of shinjin.

name: The three Pure Land sūtras and one treatise

definitions.definition: Hōnen designates the Larger Sūtra, the Contemplation Sūtra and the Amitābha Sūtra with Vasubandhu's treatise as the canon on which the Pure Land school rests (Senchakushū 1).
The Larger Sūtra is the true teaching; the other two have a surface and a hidden meaning.

name: The five sūtras and one treatise (Chinese Pure Land canon)

definitions.definition: Later Chinese Pure Land adds to the three sūtras the Samantabhadra conduct-and-vows chapter and the Śūraṅgama chapter on Mahāsthāmaprāpta's penetration through recollection, with Vasubandhu's treatise.

notes: Grouping attributed to Wei Yuan (four sūtras) and Yinguang (fifth) — recalled, not checked.

name: The patriarchs of the Lotus (Pure Land) school

definitions.definition: Zongxiao (1200) names Huiyuan the first patriarch with five successors (Shandao, Fazhao, Shaokang, Shengchang, Zongze); Zhipan (1269) names seven (Huiyuan, Shandao, Chengyuan, Fazhao, Shaokang, Yanshou, Shengchang); later lists add Zhuhong, Ouyi, Xingce, Shixian, Jixing and Yinguang for thirteen.

notes: The thirteen-patriarch list is the modern standard (recalled); the Song lists are read locally.

name: The seven masters of Jōdo Shinshū (shichi kōsō)

definitions.definition: Nāgārjuna, Vasubandhu, Tanluan, Daochuo, Shandao, Genshin and Hōnen, through whom the teaching of the primal vow was transmitted from India through China to Japan.

name: Lotus societies (lianshe) for recitation

definitions.definition: Associations of monks and lay people vowing together to be born in the West, from Huiyuan's vow of 402 to Shengchang's society, Zongze's Lotus assembly and Mao Ziyuan's repentance halls.

name: Teacher and disciple in Shinshū

definitions.definition: Shinran 'has not a single disciple', for people say the nenbutsu by Amida's working; yet he entrusts himself wholly to Hōnen's teaching; the Tannishō is not to be shown to those without karmic roots.

name: The restriction on showing the Senchakushū

definitions.definition: Hōnen asked that the Senchakushū be buried in the wall after reading, lest slanderers see it; copying was permitted only to chosen disciples (Shinran in 1205).

name: The fivefold transmission (gojū sōden)

definitions.definition: Jōdo-shū's rite of transmitting the teaching in five stages of texts and oral instruction to monks and lay people, systematised in the Chinzei line (Shōgei).

notes: Structure recalled only in outline; no text read.

name: The twelve lights of Amitābha

definitions.definition: Amitābha is called by twelve names of light — immeasurable, boundless, unhindered, incomparable, flame-king, pure, joy, wisdom, uninterrupted, inconceivable, ineffable, surpassing sun and moon (Larger Sūtra, praised by Tanluan).
The true Buddha is the Tathāgata of inconceivable light; Shinran's Jōdo wasan praise the twelve lights.

name: The bodies of those born in Sukhāvatī

definitions.definition: Beings born there appear by transformation in lotuses, all golden in colour, with the thirty-two marks, no difference between gods and humans, superknowledges and life without limit (vows; Nāgārjuna's verses); none of them is a woman or lacks faculties.

name: Four kinds of nianfo

definitions.definition: Calling the name, contemplating an image, contemplating the Buddha's marks, and recollecting the real mark (the Buddha as reality) — a later Chinese classification (attributed to Zongmi).

notes: Attribution to Zongmi recalled, not checked.

name: Faith and practice (faith, vow, practice)

definitions.definition: Faith, vow and holding the name are the three provisions for birth: whether one is born depends on faith and vow, the grade on the depth of practice (Ouyi); faith is the source of the way (Wang Rixiu).
Believe that birth is attained with one calling, yet practise with the whole of life (Hōnen).
Practice (gyō: the name) and entrusting (shin: shinjin) are both Amida's gift and are inseparable; shinjin is the cause and the nenbutsu its expression in gratitude.

relations.note: Chinese 'faith' is the practitioner's; Shinran's shinjin is given
